bihar_raw_news.content: 16th Finance Commission formula gives excessive weight to GSDP than need: UP finance minister Uttar Pradesh Finance Minister Suresh Kumar Khanna said the higher weight for GDP contribution and lower weight for income distance could favour states with stronger output, potentially reducing transfers to states with larger populations and greater fiscal needs. By PTI September 24, 2026, 6:05:23 PM IST (Published) 3 Min Read Uttar Pradesh Finance Minister Suresh Kumar Khanna on Thursday flagged concerns over the 16th Finance Commission’s devolution formula, saying the new criteria give greater importance to contribution to the GDP compared to a state’s need and could result in relatively lower transfers to high-population states. ”The principal concern is that the new criterion gives greater importance to output compared with need,” Khanna said while addressing the 13th SBI Banking & Economics Conclave 2026. He said there was a concern that states with higher GSDP could benefit under the new framework, while states such as Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh, which have larger populations and greater needs, could receive relatively less devolution. ”There is a concern that states with higher GSDP, along with two other states, could benefit, while states such as Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh, which have larger populations and greater needs, could receive relatively less devolution,” he said. Khanna said several parameters adopted by the 16th Finance Commission were ”quite alarming”, pointing to the increase in the weight assigned to contribution to GDP to 10 per cent and reduction in the weight of income distance from 45% to 42.5%. ”The weight assigned to contribution to GDP has been increased to 10%, replacing the earlier tax-effort criterion,” he said. Khanna said states should not be viewed merely as administrative units but as key drivers of India’s economic development. ”Therefore, states need to be empowered not merely as administrative units but as partners and drivers of India’s development story,” he said. He said states play a central role in managing schools, hospitals, roads, local infrastructure, agricultural support and public welfare services, and therefore require adequate and predictable resources. The Centre has fixed the states’ share in divisible tax revenues at 41% for 2026-27 to 2030-31. The 16th Finance Commission, headed by Arvind Panagariya, submitted its report on November 17, 2025. The report was tabled in Parliament on February 1, 2026. Khanna also pointed to the fiscal pressure faced by states and said the combined liabilities of the 28 states had reached ₹90.51 lakh crore in 2024-25. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Cabinet approves new sugar mill at Warisaliganj - ChiniMandi
bihar_raw_news.content: All News English Indian Sugar News Sugar News Top News Trendings AI Representational Image Patna : The Bihar Cabinet has approved a proposal to set up a new sugar mill at Warisaliganj in Nawada district, a move expected to bring an investment of more than ₹500 crore to the region, Patna Press reported. The decision was taken at the Cabinet meeting on September 23, 2026. Chief Minister Samrat Chaudhary announced the approval through social media. The proposed mill is expected to benefit sugarcane growers in Nawada, Nalanda, Sheikhpura and Jamui districts by providing them with a nearby facility to process and sell their produce. The project is also expected to generate direct and indirect employment in the region after the mill starts operations. Preparatory work for the project has been in progress for several months. On April 1, senior officials from the Bihar Sugarcane Industries Department and the local administration inspected land identified at Makanpur in Warisaliganj. More than 100 acres had been identified for the project, and the inspection was carried out to assess the availability, status and suitability of the land. The district administration subsequently prepared the necessary documents and sent the proposal to the Sugarcane Industries Department. As per the administrative proposal, around 102 acres and seven decimals of land have been identified at Makanpur. The land includes government-owned land and around 12 acres of private raiyati land. The details were prepared based on a report from local revenue officials and submitted along with maps and other documents. The proposal to establish or revive a sugar mill at Warisaliganj has been under discussion for some time. Nawada MP Vivek Thakur had raised the issue at the Centre and sought steps to restart the sugar mill. He had also suggested involving Indian Potash Limited (IPL) in its operation. The State government has also been examining proposals related to the establishment and revival of sugar mills in Bihar. A high-level review meeting chaired by Chief Secretary Pratyaya Amrit had considered the progress of proposed sugar mill projects, with the Sugarcane Industries Department presenting details of the plans. The Warisaliganj sugar mill has a long history. It was established in 1952 during the tenure of Bihar’s first Chief Minister, Dr Sri Krishna Singh, and was also known as Mohini Sugar Works. The mill was once an important industrial unit in the region and supported sugarcane cultivation among farmers in southern Bihar. The Bihar State Sugar Corporation took over the mill in 1977. However, the unit later faced financial problems, outdated technology and management issues before shutting down in 1993. The Cabinet approval has renewed expectations of sugar-based industrial activity returning to Warisaliganj. If the project is implemented, farmers in the surrounding districts could get a nearby market and processing facility for their sugarcane. The mill could also support other businesses and create employment in the area. The economic impact of the project will depend on its construction, commissioning and subsequent operations. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar CM directs long-term Kosi flood management strategy, fast-tracks solarisation, major ...
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar CM directs long-term Kosi flood management strategy, fast-tracks solarisation, major infrastructure projects ANI | Updated: Sep 24, 2026 15:50 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Patna (Bihar) [India], September 24 (ANI): Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Chaudhary on Thursday directed officials to prepare a long-term flood risk mitigation strategy for the Kosi river system, with a focus on silt management and construction of a new barrage, while reviewing major projects related to water resources, road connectivity and energy sectors. According to the Chief Minister's Office, he chaired a review meeting on major projects concerning the Ganga, Gandak and Kosi river systems, the Buxar-Bhagalpur 6-lane Greenfield Expressway, the 2400 MW (3x800 MW) Pirpainti Thermal Power Project and the PM-KUSUM scheme. The Chief Minister also issued directions to expedite the solarisation of agricultural feeders and operate state-owned tubewells through solar energy. During the review of the Kosi river system, CM Chaudhary said that the river is a "dynamic and interconnected river system" and stressed that management efforts should not remain limited to annual flood responses but should follow a long-term flood risk mitigation approach. He directed officials to adopt a holistic strategy by considering the Kosi region as a multi-district river corridor involving people, assets and connectivity. The Chief Minister emphasised the need for special attention towards silt management and instructed officials to initiate necessary action for the construction of a new barrage, as per the CMO. While reviewing the Gandak river project, CM Chaudhary directed officials to work towards installing solar plants on embankments. The Chief Minister also reviewed the progress of the Buxar-Bhagalpur 6-lane Greenfield Expressway. The total length of the project is 348.196 km, of which 336.205 km falls in Bihar and around 12 km lies in Uttar Pradesh. He further reviewed the progress of Ganga-Ambika Path (Bidupur-Dighwara), Narayani Path (Darihara-Dumaria Ghat) and Vishwamitra Path (Buxar-Ara-Maner), directing officials to accelerate implementation and ensure completion within stipulated timelines. According to the CMO, during the Energy Department review, progress of the Pirpainti Thermal Power Project with a capacity of 3x800 MW was discussed. The status of work related to the Banka Thermal Power Plant was also reviewed. The Chief Minister also took stock of the progress of solarising agricultural feeders under the PM-KUSUM scheme and directed officials to complete the work at the earliest. He highlighted the importance of promoting solar energy while ensuring adequate and reliable electricity supply to the agricultural sector. He further instructed officials to speed up efforts to run state-owned tubewells using solar energy. As per the CMO, CM Chaudhary said that an action plan must be prepared to achieve a permanent solution for flood management. He called for systematic management of the Ganga, Kosi and Gandak river s, including strengthening embankments on both sides and constructing four-lane roads over them. "The objective is to provide permanent relief to flood-affected populations in these river basins while transforming the region into a prosperous area," the Chief Minister said. He also stressed the need for 'double sheet piling'

bihar_raw_news.title: CJI Surya Kant To Inaugurate Victim Rights Centre On Single Window System Model At ...
bihar_raw_news.content: CJI Surya Kant To Inaugurate Victim Rights Centre On Single Window System Model At Patna On Sept 26 By - LIVELAW NEWS NETWORK Update: 2026-09-24 07:16 GMT Image By: Siddharth Anand Click the Play button to listen to article The Chief Justice of India, Justice Surya Kant , will inaugurate the Victim Rights Centre at the Bihar State Legal Services Authority (BSLSA), Patna , on September 26, 2026 . On the same occasion, the Chief Justice will also launch a Transgender Helpline , flag off a fleet of Multi Utility Vehicles , and release a publication on the Centre. The Centre has been established as a pilot project under Section 12 of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 . Victims of crime often have to engage with multiple institutions, including police stations, hospitals, courts and government departments, each operating through separate procedures. Various rights and entitlements are available under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 , the Bihar Victim Compensation Scheme, 2014 , and allied laws, including emergency medical treatment, legal aid, copies of FIRs, participation in bail proceedings, compensation, protection measures and appellate remedies. However, support mechanisms are presently spread across District Legal Services Authorities, District Criminal Injuries Compensation Boards, police authorities, One Stop Centres, welfare departments, hospitals and non-governmental organisations. The Centre seeks to provide a single point of entry for victims, maintain a unified case record and function through prescribed internal timelines. Cases are to remain open until relief is obtained and verified or until closure is sought in writing. The project does not create a new statutory body and operates through existing infrastructure, personnel and coordination with police authorities, hospitals, Child Welfare Committees, One Stop Centres, State departments and organisations already working in the field. The Centre is intended to facilitate and monitor access to available rights and services and does not itself disburse compensation. It may be noted that the Kerala State Legal Services Authority is also operating a Victim Rights Centre under its legal services framework, albeit on a different model. The Bihar initiative seeks to introduce a single-window system through which victims can access and coordinate multiple entitlements and services from a single point of contact. The project has been developed under the guidance of Justice V. Kameswar Rao , Chief Justice of the Patna High Court and Patron-in-Chief of the Authority, and Justice Sudhir Singh , Judge of the Patna High Court and Executive Chairman of the Authority. Policy oversight is vested in a Steering Committee chaired by a Judge of the Patna High Court, with Justice Ajeet Kumar serving as its first Chairman. A Coordination Committee comprising representatives of relevant departments and agencies will oversee inter-departmental implementation, while administrative control rests with the Member Secretary of the Authority. Recognition Of 'Situational Victims' The Centre also proposes maintaining records relating to "situational victims". This category includes dependent family members of sole earning undertrial prisoners whose prolonged incarceration results in loss of income, disruption of education, delayed medical treatment and loss of property.

bihar_raw_news.content: Blog Rooftop Solar Subsidies Get a Fresh Push Across Tamil Nadu, Delhi and Bihar Delhi, Bihar, and Tamil Nadu have adopted distinct approaches but share the common goal of providing additional incentives that aim to reduce the upfront cost of rooftop solar and accelerate distributed solar adoption among households. Chitrika Grover 24 Sep 2026 08:49 IST Follow Us Delhi, Bihar and Tamil Nadu have introduced or approved additional financial incentives for residential rooftop solar installations under the PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana, adding state-level support to the central subsidy available to consumers. Advertisment Delhi, Bihar and Tamil Nadu have adopted distinct approaches to supplementing the central subsidy under PM Surya Ghar. While the three states are taking different approaches, the additional incentives aim to reduce the upfront cost of rooftop solar and accelerate distributed solar adoption among households. Advertisment Delhi is providing the largest direct top-up, offering an additional ₹78,000 to eligible households with average monthly electricity consumption below 400 units, while also extending support to Group Housing Societies. Bihar is providing additional state incentives of up to ₹20,000 for a 3 kW system, taking the combined support under the central and state schemes to as much as ₹98,000, while linking rooftop solar with its wider decentralised renewable-energy and solarisation plans. Advertisment Tamil Nadu, meanwhile, has earmarked ₹50 crore to support rooftop solar installations for 1 lakh domestic consumers, with state subsidies ranging from ₹5,000 for systems up to 1 kW to ₹22,000 for systems of 3 kW and above. Delhi Offers Additional Subsidy for Households Using Less Than 400 Units Advertisment The Delhi government has extended an additional rooftop solar subsidy of ₹78,000 under its Top-up Solar (ToP) Scheme, in addition to the subsidy already available under the PM Surya Ghar scheme. The second round of the subsidy targets consumers with an average monthly electricity consumption of less than 400 units. Eligible consumers can have a rooftop solar plant installed without paying the installation cost, subject to the scheme's conditions. Advertisment The Delhi government has also extended the benefits of the ToP Scheme to Group Housing Societies (GHSs). As part of the implementation, the government plans to empanel solar vendors for installing rooftop solar systems of up to 3 kW under the Utility-Led Aggregation (ULA)/Discom Trusteeship Model. Selected vendors will visit eligible consumers' premises after receiving their consent. Bihar Adds State Incentive to PM Surya Ghar Subsidy Bihar has also introduced additional incentives for residential rooftop solar installations through its Mukhyamantri Solar Protsahan Yojana. The state government's additional support is designed to supplement the central financial assistance available under PM Surya Ghar. The combined support can take the subsidy available for a 3 kW rooftop solar system to up to ₹98,000, according to the state government's announcement. Under the structure outlined for the scheme, the central subsidy provides ₹30,000 for a 1 kW system, ₹60,000 for a 2 kW system and ₹78,000 for systems of 3 kW and above. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Cabinet approves Mata Sita, Ramdhari Singh Dinkar universities - Daily Excelsior
bihar_raw_news.content: Advertisement Home / National / Bihar Cabinet approves Mata Sita, Ramdhari Singh Dinkar universities Bihar Cabinet approves Mata Sita, Ramdhari Singh Dinkar universities PATNA, Sep 23 : The Bihar Cabinet on Wednesday approved the establishment of Mata Sita University in Patna and Rashtra Kavi Ramdhari Singh Dinkar University in Begusarai. The decisions were taken at a Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Samrat... Daily Excelsior 04:29 AM Sep 24, 2026 IST PATNA, Sep 23 : The Bihar Cabinet on Wednesday approved the establishment of Mata Sita University in Patna and Rashtra Kavi Ramdhari Singh Dinkar University in Begusarai. The decisions were taken at a Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary. Additional Cabinet Secretary Arvind Kumar Choudhary told news persons after the meeting that the Cabinet approved Rs 15 crore each for the establishment of the two universities to meet expenditure on salaries and other establishment-related requirements. Advertisement The proposed university in Patna was initially referred to as Maa Sita University, but the Cabinet approved an amendment changing the name to Mata Sita University. The cabinet also cleared a slew of proposals involving police modernisation, dairy and fisheries development, power sector liabilities and prison reforms. Among the major decisions, the Cabinet sanctioned Rs 24.50 crore for procurement of 50 drones under the centrally sponsored scheme for assistance to states and union Territories for police modernisation. The drones are intended for crowd-control and management, riverine and anti-Naxal operations, disaster management and other policing requirements, 8nforned Choudhary. An additional Rs 33.685 crore was approved for procurement of equipment and other items for district police, railway police, the Bihar Special Armed Police, the Prohibition Department and the State Narcotics Control Bureau, among other agencies. The Cabinet also approved a one-time remission measure for eligible convicted prisoners to facilitate their release from jails on the occasion of Mahatma Gandhi''s birth anniversary on October 2, 2026. It further approved amendments to Rule 743 of the Bihar Prison Manual, 2012, in accordance with the Supreme Court''s orders of July 30 and September 10, 2026, in the case concerning discrimination inside prisons. For the agriculture and livestock sector, the Cabinet approved the state scheme Mukhyamantri Gaudhan Vikas Rin Yojana for 2026-27 to 2028-29, involving an estimated expenditure of Rs 160.001 crore. The government also approved release of Rs 757.63 crore to Bihar State Power (Holding) Company Ltd in five equal instalments towards unfunded terminal benefit liabilities of former Bihar State Electricity Board employees up to October 31, 2012. Under Saat Nischay-3, the Cabinet approved a Rs 126.07-crore dairy development programme in Supaul, Madhepura and Saharsa districts. The programme includes setting up a curd plant, premium ice-cream plant, Total Mixed Ration plant, buffalo heifer farm, use of sex-sorted semen, formation of new dairy cooperative societies and installation of milk chilling infrastructure. A Rs 195.28-crore project under the Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF) was also approved for transforming the Siwan wetlands cluster in Basantpur, Bhagwanpur Hat and Goriakothi into an integrated aquaculture and export-oriented value chain.

bihar_raw_news.title: Beyond Jamui - The Statesman
bihar_raw_news.content: Subscribe to Notifications The assault on two school students ~ a girl and a boy, both teenagers ~ in Bihar’s Jamui district is a test of more than policing. It challenges the social assumption that a young woman’s movements and associations are subject to scrutiny, and sometimes punishment, by men who appoint themselves guardians of morality. The violence against the girl and her male friend demands accountability, but the circumstances also expose a deeper struggle over personal freedom and dignity. The reported arrests, formation of a special investigation team and police action are necessary steps. Yet the case has also raised questions about how the authorities learned of the assault. The teenagers reportedly did not initially approach the police; investigators traced them after footage circulated online. This sequence deserves examination, without presuming that the victims’ silence reflects any failure. Shame, fear of exposure and concern about family or social consequences can complicate reporting, especially for minors. The circulation of the footage compounds the original violation. A recording intended to expose wrongdoing can become another instrument of humiliation when it reveals the identities of children. Action against accounts sharing the clips is therefore not a peripheral digital exercise. It is part of protecting the victims. The National Commission for Women’s intervention should reinforce the obligation to safeguard their privacy, rather than allow public outrage to turn into a second ordeal. The political response has been equally revealing. Describing such episodes as isolated incidents may be statistically defensible, but the phrase cannot substitute for evidence or answer public anxiety. Conversely, opposition leaders cannot establish a government’s overall failure through one disturbing case. Bihar’s record on women’s safety must be judged through credible data on violence, reporting, investigation, prosecution and conviction, alongside the accessibility of support for victims. The central issue, however, extends beyond party politics. If the assault arose from disapproval of two teenagers being together, it represents an attempt to enforce social conformity through intimidation. No private group has the authority to police another person’s relationships or movements. The state’s responsibility is to protect that freedom, not merely to punish its violent violation after the event. The reported arrest of suspects is a development, not the conclusion of the case. Investigators must establish each accused person’s role, preserve evidence and proceed through due process. Any alleged police encounter must also be subject to appropriate scrutiny; accountability cannot depend on the spectacle of force. Jamui should prompt more than expressions of shame or demands for exemplary punishment. It should lead to practical questions: Can minors report harassment safely? Are police equipped to respond sensitively? Are victims protected from exposure and intimidation? And can authorities demonstrate, through outcomes rather than assurances, that public spaces belong to girls as much as to boys? The measure of justice will not be the volume of outrage, but whether the teenagers regain their privacy and security ~ and whether the institutions responsible for protecting them learn from the assault. national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi today said that service should be the main purpose of life and must be inherent in every individual. He said that in politics too, service should remain the guiding principle, even when one reaches the highest position. Mr Modi made these remarks during a virtual interaction with Seva Yatris travelling on the Yatra from Vadnagar to Varanasi. The Prime Minister said, ‘Seva Paramo Dharma’ service is the highest duty should remain the guiding principle. Mr Modi said, service is the biggest driving force. He said, whether it is PM-KISAN or the PM Surya Ghar Yojana, countless such schemes are recognised for their last-mile delivery. The Prime Minister said, it is only when there is a spirit of service, four crore poor have receive permanent houses. He said, when the spirit of service is integrated into a nation’s policies, service itself becomes the greatest driving force for the country’s progress. Mr Modi said, it gives rise to innovative schemes that bring out 25 crore citizens from the cycle of poverty. He said, politics, elections, and systems of governance have their own place. The Prime Minister said, we are people dedicated to nation-building and set out with the resolve to build a developed India. He said, everyone must vigorously advance the pivotal role of the youth in building a developed India by 2047. Mr Modi said, today’s young generation is both the architect of a developed India and the one that will be a major beneficiary of it. During the interaction, Seva Yatris shared their experiences with the Prime Minister. They said that they planted saplings and conducted cleanliness drives as part of the campaign. They added that during the yatra, they interacted with people and received their positive feedback on the benefits of various government schemes.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi also congratulated Naorem Roshibina Devi on winning the Silver Medal in the Women’s Sanda 60kg event at the Asian Games. In a social media post, Mr Modi said that winning medals at three consecutive Asian Games is a remarkable achievement. He said that Naorem Roshibina’s consistency, courage and determination are truly commendable. Mr Modi congratulated Satnam Singh and Salman Khan on winning the bronze medal in the Men’s Double Sculls at the Asian Games. In a social media post, he said that the performance by both athletes has earned India a well-deserved medal. Prime Minister Modi said that their composure and coordination stood out. He stated that this accomplishment will serve as motivation for them to attain even greater heights in the year ahead.

national_raw_news.title: Mizoram launches first ‘Pluck & Pay’ festival to boost rural tourism 23 mins ago 14
national_raw_news.content: Mizoram has launched its first ‘Pluck & Pay’ festival in Khawzawl district in the eastern part of the state, offering visitors an opportunity to harvest farm produce themselves and pay farmers directly as the state seeks to expand tourism-led livelihood opportunities in rural communities, officials said. The three-day festival, being held from September 23 to 25 at Tualte and Chawngtlai villages, has been jointly organised by the state Tourism department and the office of the Khawzawl Deputy Commissioner. The initiative brings agriculture, horticulture, tourism, local food and community enterprise together, allowing visitors to experience rural life while creating direct economic linkages with farming households, officials said. Tourism Minister Lalnghinglova Hmar said the initiative reflected the state’s broader vision of ensuring that tourism benefits the communities hosting visitors. “The future of tourism is not only about taking visitors to places; it is about creating value for the people who make those places worth visiting,” he said, adding that the government wanted stronger linkages between tourism and villages, farms, entrepreneurs and cultural communities. Besides farm visits and harvesting, the festival features traditional Mizo music and dance, local cuisine, handicrafts, cultural performances and traditional recreational games, besides visits to historical and tourist sites. The initiative is aimed at creating an ecosystem in which tourism spending can also support local farmers, homestays, guides, transport operators, artisans and other community-based enterprises. The launch marks the beginning of Mizoram’s 2026 festival season, with the Anthurium Festival at Reiek, Hnahsin Kût in Champhai and Travel Fest in Aizawl among the events lined up in the coming months. Leitlangpui Music Festival, Winter Festival, Tlaizawng Paradise Festival and Sakawrhmuituai Sunset Event are also scheduled as part of the wider tourism calendar. Official figures presented during the recent state assembly session showed tourist arrivals rising from 4,27,302 in 2024 to 8,41,322 in 2025. The ‘Pluck & Pay’ initiative seeks to leverage this growing visitor base to increase the participation of rural communities in the state’s tourism economy, officials added.

national_raw_news.title: Ministry of Culture will organise BRICS Theatre Festival 2026 from October 12 to 14 October
national_raw_news.content: Ministry of Culture will organise BRICS Theatre Festival 2026 from October 12 to 14 October Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Ministry of Culture will organise BRICS Theatre Festival 2026 from October 12 to 14 October ANI | Updated: Sep 24, 2026 20:12 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], September 24 (ANI): The Ministry of Culture will organise the BRICS Theatre Festival 2026 from 12 to 14 October 2026 in New Delhi under India’s BRICS Presidency 2026. The three-day festival, themed “Shared Stories, Shared Futures”, will bring together over 100 theatre practitioners, scholars, students and cultural representatives from nine BRICS Member and Partner Countries. Addressing the media, Vivek Aggarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Culture, highlighted its significance as an important cultural engagement under India’s BRICS Presidency and its role in advancing people-to-people connections through theatre. The Secretary said that the festival builds on the Bhopal Declaration adopted at the BRICS Culture Ministers’ Meeting in August 2026, which emphasised greater cultural cooperation, people-to-people exchanges and stronger networks among artists and cultural practitioners. India also proposed a voluntary Artist Registry to facilitate such exchanges. The festival carries this vision forward through performances and professional interactions among theatre practitioners from BRICS countries, he added. The significance of the festival has also been recognised in the BRICS Leaders’ Declaration, which welcomed the Bhopal Declaration and noted initiatives aimed at strengthening cultural cooperation, cultural exchanges and people-to-people ties. The festival will feature participation from India, Thailand, Indonesia, Russia, Vietnam, Iran, South Africa, Kazakhstan and Ethiopia. India will showcase two theatre productions, while the participating countries will present productions reflecting their diverse languages, theatrical traditions and contemporary creative expressions. Russia will be represented by two theatre groups. The festival will be inaugurated at the National School of Drama on 12 October 2026. Performances will be staged at prominent theatre venues in New Delhi, including the National School of Drama and its Abhimanch Auditorium and Sammukh Auditorium, along with Kamani Auditorium, LTG Auditorium and Meghdoot Theatre. The festival will showcase classical, contemporary and experimental forms of theatre. Interactive workshops and discussions involving directors, artistes and production teams will provide opportunities for exchange on artistic vision, performance traditions, acting methodologies, stagecraft and technical design. The National School of Drama, an autonomous institution under the Ministry of Culture, will serve as the nodal agency for organising the festival. The BRICS Theatre Festival 2026 seeks to strengthen cultural cooperation and people-to-people connections among BRICS countries by bringing together artistes, theatre practitioners and audiences through a shared artistic platform. national_raw_news.content: Ministry of Railways Indian Railways Approves New Daily Train Service Between Kanpur Central and Anand Vihar (T) Daily Overnight Service to Enhance Passenger Connectivity Between Kanpur and Delhi, Serving Etawah, Aligarh, Ghaziabad and Other Key Stations Posted On: 24 SEP 2026 3:17PM by PIB Delhi Indian Railways has approved the introduction of a new daily train service between Kanpur Central and Anand Vihar (T), providing an overnight rail connectivity option between Kanpur and Delhi. The new service will operate as Train No. 14153/14154 Kanpur Central-Anand Vihar (T)-Kanpur Central Mail. Convenient Overnight Journey Between Kanpur and Delhi Train No. 14153 Kanpur Central-Anand Vihar (T) Mail will depart from Kanpur Central at 20:40 hours and reach Anand Vihar (T) at 04:50 hours the next morning. In the return direction, Train No. 14154 Anand Vihar (T)-Kanpur Central Mail will depart from Anand Vihar (T) at 23:25 hours and arrive at Kanpur Central at 07:25 hours. The service will cover a distance of 428 km in both directions. The journey time will be 8 hours 10 minutes from Kanpur Central to Anand Vihar (T), and 8 hours in the return direction. Daily Service with Eight Commercial Stoppages The new train service will have commercial stoppages at: Phaphund Etawah Tundla Hathras Aligarh Khurja Dadri Ghaziabad The daily service will provide passengers with an additional rail travel option between Kanpur and the National Capital Region, with convenient overnight timings in both directions. Strengthening Passenger Connectivity The introduction of the new daily Mail service will strengthen rail connectivity between Kanpur Central and Anand Vihar (T) while providing passengers with an overnight travel option and connectivity to important stations along the route. The service will facilitate convenient movement between Kanpur, Etawah, Aligarh, Ghaziabad and the Delhi region, supporting passenger mobility across this important rail corridor. ***** Dharmendra Tewari/ Dr. Nayan Solanki/ Ritu Raj (Release ID: 2314361) Visitor Counter : 496 Read this release in: Urdu , हिन्दी , Gujarati , Tamil , Telugu , Kannada Ministry of Railways Indian Railways Approves New Daily Train Service Between Kanpur Central and Anand Vihar (T) Daily Overnight Service to Enhance Passenger Connectivity Between Kanpur and Delhi, Serving Etawah, Aligarh, Ghaziabad and Other Key Stations Posted On: 24 SEP 2026 3:17PM by PIB Delhi Indian Railways has approved the introduction of a new daily train service between Kanpur Central and Anand Vihar (T), providing an overnight rail connectivity option between Kanpur and Delhi. national_raw_news.title: FSSAI proposes draft amendment to ensure only milk-derived products are represented as 'Paneer'
national_raw_news.content: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare FSSAI proposes draft amendment to ensure only milk-derived products are represented as ‘Paneer’ FSSAI Moves to Curb Misleading Marketing of Analogue Products as ‘Paneer’, Proposes Ban on Use of ‘Paneer’ Term for Non-Milk-Derived Products Posted On: 24 SEP 2026 7:23PM by PIB Delhi The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has proposed a draft amendment to the Food Safety and Standards (Prohibition and Restrictions on Sales) Regulations, 2011, to restrict the manufacture and sale of analogue products as “Paneer” and prevent consumers from being misled about the nature and composition of such products. The proposed Food Safety and Standards (Prohibition and Restrictions on Sales) Amendment Regulations, 2026 seek to insert a new clause under Regulation 2.1.1 of the existing regulations, specifically covering “paneer made of constituents not derived from milk.” Under the proposed amendment, products already licensed or registered under the ‘Analogue in Dairy Context’ category would be required to discontinue the use of the term “Paneer” in their nomenclature, labelling or marketing. The proposed amendment is aimed at ensuring that the nomenclature and presentation of food products accurately reflect their nature and composition, thereby enabling consumers to make informed choices. As the notification is a draft regulation, FSSAI has invited objections and suggestions from stakeholders and members of the public. The draft regulations will be taken into consideration after the expiry of 60 days from the date on which copies of the Official Gazette containing the notification are made available to the public. Objections or suggestions may be addressed to the Chief Executive Officer, Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), FDA Bhawan, Kotla Road, New Delhi – 110002, or submitted through the email address specified in the notification. The proposed amendment has been issued by FSSAI with the previous approval of the Central Government under the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. The principal Food Safety and Standards (Prohibition and Restrictions on Sales) Regulations were notified in 2011 and have been amended from time to time. national_raw_news.title: PIB Media Delegation Visits South Regu to Witness Large Cardamom Cultivation in Sikkim
national_raw_news.content: Government of Sikkim, India My Government Other Links News & Announcement News & Announcement PIB Media Delegation Visits South Regu to Witness Large Cardamom Cultivation in Sikkim Date: 16-Sep-2026 Pakyong, September 16th (IPR): A media delegation from the Press Information Bureau (PIB), Himachal Pradesh, visited South Regu village in Pakyong District today as part of its field visit to gain first-hand insight into Sikkim’s agricultural practices, with a special focus on the cultivation and production of large cardamom. During the visit, Senior Scientist, Spices Board, Dr Tikendra Deka, provided a detailed briefing on large cardamom cultivation and production in Sikkim. He apprised the delegation of the crop’s cultivation practices and its significance to the State’s agricultural landscape. The delegation also interacted with large cardamom cultivators and Panchayat members, gaining insights into farmers' experiences, prevailing cultivation practices, and grassroots-level challenges. The field interaction provided the visiting media delegation an opportunity to understand the role of large cardamom cultivation in supporting the rural economy and livelihoods of farming communities in Sikkim. The visit also highlighted the importance of documenting and showcasing successful agricultural practices and farming communities' experiences through media outreach, thereby giving wider visibility to Sikkim’s distinctive agricultural produce and grassroots development initiatives. national_raw_news.title: Media delegation from Bhopal visits AIIMS Vijaypur, Bahu Fort Aquarium - Daily Excelsior
national_raw_news.content: Media delegation from Bhopal visits AIIMS Vijaypur, Bahu Fort Aquarium - Daily Excelsior Menu Todays story Latest News State Business National International Editorials Sunday Magazine State National Business Opinion Sports International Sunday Magazine J&K Govt Orders Videos Employment Prof (Dr) Sanjeev Sinha, Director & CEO, AIIMS Vijaypur, posing with visiting media delegation from Bhopal. Excelsior Correspondent JAMMU, Sept 23: A delegation of media persons from Bhopal, on an exposure tour organized by the Press Information Bureau (PIB), today visited AIIMS Vijaypur in Samba district, and the Aquarium-cum-Awareness Centre at Bahu Fort, Jammu, to gain first-hand insight into major infrastructure, healthcare, academic and developmental initiatives in the region. At AIIMS Vijaypur, the delegation interacted with senior faculty and officials and was briefed on the institute’s expanding clinical, academic and research activities. Prof (Dr) Sanjeev Sinha, Director & CEO, AIIMS Vijaypur, said the institute has a 750-bed capacity, including 650 fixed beds, modern modular operation theatres, a fully equipped emergency medicine block and an integrated AYUSH Centre. He said the hospital is witnessing a daily OPD footfall of 1,000 to 2,000 patients, averaging around 1,500, with patients arriving from Jammu & Kashmir, Punjab, Himachal Pradesh and even New Delhi. He said 30 broad specialties and 14 super-specialties, including Cardiology, Neurosurgery and Plastic Surgery, are operational, enabling comprehensive treatment locally. Prof (Dr) Shabab Lalit Angurana, Professor, Dean of Research, and HoD Radiotherapy & Oncology, said the institute, which started with 50 MBBS seats, is admitting 125 students in the current batch. It is also running MD programmes and 50 super-specialty seats, including M Ch in Pediatric Surgery and DM in Endocrinology, while PhD programmes are expected to commence soon. Prof (Dr) Vijay Kundal, Dr Amit Chaudhary, Assistant Professor, Department of Hospital Administration, and other senior administrative and clinical officers were present. Later, the delegation visited the Aquarium-cum-Awareness Centre at Bahu Fort, where Joint Director, Department of Fisheries, Masood Hussain, briefed them on sectoral initiatives. Spread over 30 kanals, the Rs 8.40-crore Phase-I facility houses the country’s largest freshwater aquarium with over 100 fish species and attracts visitors throughout the year. The delegation was informed that the ongoing Phase-II includes North India’s first and India’s third marine aquarium, scheduled to open in November, featuring a 4-lakh-litre marine water system, 50-mm acrylic glass with 98 per cent transparency and 18,000 kg of specialized salt.
